accepted.s: The Central Vigilance Commission acquired statutory status through the
accepted.x: The CVC was made a statutory body by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
accepted.tq: Use the exact Act associated with the change from executive body to statutory body.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The statutory status of the Central Vigilance Commission followed, in the relevant sequence, the
accepted.x: The CVC became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003, after the Vineet Narain judgment of 1997.
accepted.tq: Arrange the institutional developments by identifying the earlier judicial milestone and the later statute.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term of office of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and a Vigilance Commissioner is
o: four years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
five years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
four years without any age limit
six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
accepted.x: The term is four years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
accepted.tq: Separate the two limiting conditions—tenure and age—before choosing the complete provision.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the Central Vigilance Commission, which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: It recommends the Director of Prosecution of the CBI.
It directly conducts the trial of all corruption cases investigated by the CBI.
Its committee recommends CBI officers of the rank of Superintendent of Police and above.
It exercises superintendence over the CBI in cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
accepted.x: The CVC exercises specified superintendence and makes recommendations, but it does not conduct the trials of CBI corruption cases.
accepted.tq: Find the option that assigns a judicial trial function to a vigilance body.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As on 31 December 2025, the number of CBI cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act pending trial was reported as
accepted.x: The reported figure was 7,229 CBI cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act pending trial as on 31 December 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the precise date with the precise institutional figure rather than confusing it with annual disposal or reference data.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The CBI conviction rate in 2025, as reported in the CVC Annual Report, was
accepted.x: The CBI conviction rate was 71.71 per cent in 2025, compared with 69.14 per cent in 2024.
accepted.tq: Use the year-wise comparison to distinguish the current figure from the preceding year’s figure.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many Lokpal references were pending investigation in the CVC Annual Report figure cited for 2025?
accepted.x: The report indicated that 13 Lokpal references were pending investigation.
accepted.tq: Identify the small institutional count separately from the much larger pending-trial figure.
accepted.sec: Central Vigilance Commission - origin, CVC Act 2003, status, composition, role over CBI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act was enacted in
accepted.x: The governing law is the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the founding State Act and later central anti-corruption legislation.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983 was amended by the
accepted.x: The 1983 Act was amended by the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta (Amendment) Act, 2024.
accepted.tq: Read the title carefully and distinguish the amendment year from the principal Act year.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the first Lokayukta of the integrated State of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Justice A. Sambasiva Rao was the first Lokayukta of the integrated State of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first office-holder, the present office-holder and other anti-corruption personalities.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the structure and jurisdiction of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta:
1. The Lokayukta deals with complaints against higher functionaries.
2. The Upa-Lokayukta deals with complaints against the remaining functionaries within its jurisdiction.
3. The Chief Minister and Members of the Legislative Assembly are covered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta have differentiated functions, and the stated coverage includes the Chief Minister and MLAs.
accepted.tq: Test the hierarchy of functions together with the persons included in the jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In August 2026, Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao was appointed Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh by the
o: Chief Justice of Andhra Pradesh High Court
accepted.x: Governor S. Abdul Nazeer appointed Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao under Section 3(1), on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints?’ test to distinguish the constitutional appointing authority from the recommending body.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term of office prescribed for the present Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh under Section 5 is
accepted.x: Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao was appointed for a term of five years under Section 5.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State Lokayukta tenure from the CVC tenure and age-based limit.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta annual report for 2025:
1. It handled 7,431 cases.
2. It disposed of 3,654 cases.
3. It facilitated recoveries of ₹15.29 crore.
4. It processed 148 RTI applications.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four figures are reported for the 2025 annual report: 7,431 cases handled, 3,654 disposed, ₹15.29 crore recovered and 148 RTI applications processed.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical statement independently because the figures belong to different performance indicators.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 7,431 cases handled by the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta in 2025 comprised
accepted.x: The total consisted of 3,106 fresh cases and 4,325 backlog cases.
accepted.tq: Split the aggregate into its two components instead of treating the total as the only relevant figure.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which department accounted for nearly half of the cases disposed of by the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta in 2025?
accepted.x: Nearly half of the 3,654 disposed cases related to the Revenue Department.
accepted.tq: Match the performance statistic with the department specifically associated with it.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the functioning of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta during most of 2025:
1. The post of Lokayukta remained vacant for most of the year.
2. Upa-Lokayukta P. Rajani carried out all functions during that period.
3. P. Rajani ordered payment of ₹50.24 lakh towards EPF and ESI dues to outsourced staff of 32 KGBVs in Srikakulam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The full-time post was vacant for most of 2025, P. Rajani performed the functions, and the stated order concerned EPF/ESI dues of outsourced staff in 32 KGBVs in Srikakulam.
accepted.tq: Combine the vacancy fact, acting arrangement and the specific relief order without swapping the office-holder or amount.
accepted.sec: AP Lokayukta - AP Lokayukta Act features, first Lokayukta of integrated AP  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, a whistleblower may be
o: only a Member of Parliament making a complaint to the Lokpal
only a government employee of the Union Government
a public servant or another person, including an NGO, making a public interest disclosure
accepted.x: A whistleblower includes any public servant or other person, including an NGO, who makes a public interest disclosure of specified wrongdoing to the Competent Authority.
accepted.tq: Test the inclusive definition against options that wrongly restrict the eligible complainant.
accepted.sec: Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 - definition, protections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For disclosures concerning corruption by public servants at the Centre under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, the Competent Authority is the
accepted.x: The Central Vigilance Commission is the Competent Authority for such disclosures at the Centre.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘which body receives the disclosure?’ test to distinguish vigilance, information and recruitment authorities.
accepted.sec: Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 - definition, protections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a protection or related provision under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
o: Automatic immunity from every criminal proceeding for the complainant
Punishment for false or frivolous complaints
accepted.x: The Act protects identity and guards against victimisation, while false or frivolous complaints are punishable. It does not provide automatic immunity from every criminal proceeding.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad protection that goes beyond the specified safeguards.
accepted.sec: Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014 - definition, protections  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the First Administrative Reforms Commission from the Santhanam Committee?
o: The First ARC recommended the CVC, whereas the Santhanam Committee recommended the Lokpal.
The First ARC recommended a two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta system, whereas the Santhanam Committee recommended the CVC and the CBI.
The Santhanam Committee recommended the Lokayukta for States, whereas the First ARC recommended only the CBI.
Both bodies recommended only the Lokpal at the Union level.
accepted.x: The First ARC recommended Lokpal at the Union level and Lokayukta in the States. The Santhanam Committee was associated with the CVC and the CBI, not the Lokpal.
accepted.tq: Separate closely associated anti-corruption bodies by assigning each recommendation to the correct committee.
accepted.sec: Bodies recommending Lokpal/Lokayukta - First ARC vs Santhanam Committee  [other exams]

accepted.s: The First Administrative Reforms Commission was chaired initially by
accepted.x: The First ARC was chaired by Morarji Desai during 1966–70. K. Hanumanthaiya later chaired it after Desai joined the Cabinet.
accepted.tq: Use the original chairperson and the later successor as a confusable pair.
accepted.sec: Bodies recommending Lokpal/Lokayukta - First ARC vs Santhanam Committee  [other exams]

accepted.s: The First Administrative Reforms Commission’s recommendation for redressal of citizens’ grievances envisaged
o: a single Lokpal for both the Union and the States
a two-tier system comprising Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for the States
a CVC for the Union and a CBI for the States
Lokayukta at the Union level and Lokpal in the States
accepted.x: The First ARC recommended two tiers: Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for the States, in its 1966 interim report on the Problems of Redressal of Citizens’ Grievances.
accepted.tq: Match each tier with its level of government and reject the reversed pairing.
accepted.sec: Bodies recommending Lokpal/Lokayukta - First ARC vs Santhanam Committee  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The First ARC made its two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta recommendation in 1966.
2. The Second ARC strongly reiterated the Lokpal recommendation in 2007.
3. The Santhanam Committee functioned during 1962–64.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The First ARC’s recommendation dates to 1966, the Second ARC reiterated it in 2007, and the Santhanam Committee operated during 1962–64.
accepted.tq: Anchor each statement to its committee and year before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Bodies recommending Lokpal/Lokayukta - First ARC vs Santhanam Committee  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Santhanam Committee
B. First Administrative Reforms Commission recommendation on Lokpal and Lokayukta
C. Vineet Narain judgment
D. Central Vigilance Commission Act
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Santhanam Committee (1962–64), First ARC recommendation (1966), Vineet Narain judgment (1997), and CVC Act (2003).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest committee and latest statute first, then place the 1966 and 1997 milestones between them.
accepted.sec: Bodies recommending Lokpal/Lokayukta - First ARC vs Santhanam Committee  [other exams]

accepted.s: The India Against Corruption movement was led by
accepted.x: India Against Corruption was led by Anna Hazare and was central to the 2011 civil society campaign for the Jan Lokpal Bill.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the movement’s leader from members of the later drafting committee.
accepted.sec: Civil society pressure - India Against Corruption, Anna Hazare, Jan Lokpal drafting panel  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Anna Hazare’s fasts that intensified pressure for the Jan Lokpal Bill were held at
o: Jantar Mantar in April 2011 and Ramlila Maidan in August 2011
Ramlila Maidan in April 2011 and Jantar Mantar in August 2011
Jantar Mantar in August 2011 and Ramlila Maidan in December 2011
Rajghat in April 2011 and Jantar Mantar in August 2011
accepted.x: The fasts were held at Jantar Mantar in April 2011 and at Ramlila Maidan in August 2011.
accepted.tq: Pair each venue with its correct month and reject the reversed sequence.
accepted.sec: Civil society pressure - India Against Corruption, Anna Hazare, Jan Lokpal drafting panel  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Joint Drafting Committee formed in April 2011, consider the following statements:
1. Pranab Mukherjee was the chairperson on the Government side.
2. Shanti Bhushan was the co-chairperson from the civil society side.
3. Anna Hazare, Prashant Bhushan, Arvind Kejriwal and Justice N. Santosh Hegde represented civil society.
4. P. Chidambaram, Veerappa Moily, Kapil Sibal and Salman Khurshid were on the Government side.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly identify the chairpersons and members of the Government and civil society sides of the April 2011 Joint Drafting Committee.
accepted.tq: Classify every name by side and office before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Civil society pressure - India Against Corruption, Anna Hazare, Jan Lokpal drafting panel  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
